boards.title: Your First Weekend at Florida Atlantic University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A conservative first-weekend sequence mixing campus orientation, student facilities, art, recreation, and three public Boca Raton destinations. Check linked sources before departure because schedules and access conditions can change.

cards.entity_name: Florida Atlantic University Boca Raton Campus
cards.title: Start with the campus layout
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Student Services area
cards.notes: Begin near Student Services, identify Lots 16 and 18, and use the campus visit information to establish your bearings before exploring.
cards.short_summary: An orientation stop that turns the campus map into a usable mental picture.
cards.evidence_claim: Florida Atlantic identifies 777 Glades Road as its main Boca Raton campus and places visitor parking in Lots 16 and 18 beside the Student Services Building.
cards.access_notes: In-person admissions tours require advance registration; visitor parking is metered at $2 per hour according to the source.

cards.title: Find the campus gathering point
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Student Union
cards.notes: Walk through the renovated Union, locate its service areas, and note the event spaces you may return to once the semester gets moving.
cards.short_summary: A practical first look at FAU’s central community and involvement building.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU describes the Boca Raton Student Union as its campus center for community and leadership, with programs, facilities, services, and an eSports Arena Gaming Center.
cards.access_notes: Building services and individual activities may follow separate schedules or access rules; check the Union’s current information.

cards.title: Pause for an on-campus meal
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Student Union
cards.notes: Use this stop to learn where the main dining hall sits and ask staff about dietary needs before relying on it during a busy week.
cards.short_summary: A meal break that also establishes the location of FAU’s primary dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU identifies Atlantic Dining Hall as an all-you-can-eat facility in the Boca Raton Student Union, open to the FAU community and visitors.
cards.access_notes: A meal swipe or payment is required; the official page lists Owl Card funds, meal swipes, cash, and credit cards as payment methods.

cards.title: Learn the library entry routine
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Boca Raton campus
cards.notes: Enter through the public-facing library route, find the service points, and remember that student study rooms have narrower eligibility.
cards.short_summary: A low-pressure walkthrough of the campus’s principal library and its access rules.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU Libraries provides dedicated Wimberly Library information for guests and states that study rooms are limited to currently enrolled FAU or Palm Beach State students and employees.
cards.access_notes: Public visitors should review current library hours and entry rules; student and employee eligibility applies to study-room use.

cards.title: Add a gallery stop upstairs
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Second-floor Breezeway
cards.notes: Follow campus signage to the second-floor gallery, check the current exhibition first, and pair the visit with a Breezeway walk.
cards.short_summary: A compact arts stop that introduces one of FAU’s named exhibition spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU locates Ritter Art Gallery in building AG-39 on the second floor of the Breezeway near the library and publishes visitor directions and parking guidance.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current exhibition and gallery schedule before visiting; parking charges may apply outside designated free programming periods.

cards.title: Try a short recreation session
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · North end of the Breezeway
cards.notes: Bring your Owl Card, tour the available fitness areas, and ask the Rec Desk about equipment checkout before planning a longer workout.
cards.short_summary: An active stop for learning how student recreation access works.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU says registered students receive semester access through required activity and service fees, while entry requires a valid Owl Card, membership pass, or approved scan.
cards.access_notes: Access is restricted to eligible students and members. The fitness floor requires users to be at least 18 and wear appropriate workout attire.

cards.title: Ride one campus loop
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Boca Raton shuttle route
cards.notes: Use one shuttle ride to connect landmarks you have already seen, then save the official route page for future campus crossings.
cards.short_summary: A practical transit exercise for understanding distances across the Boca Raton campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Florida Atlantic maintains an official Boca Campus Shuttle page for OwlExpress service and identifies the Breezeway among the campus route information.
cards.access_notes: Consult the official page for the current route and operating schedule before waiting; service availability can vary by academic calendar.

cards.title: Take an evening fountain walk
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · Downtown Boca Raton
cards.notes: Walk the illuminated paths, use the benches near the decorative fountains, and follow posted park rules while exploring downtown.
cards.short_summary: A public evening walk among fountains, paths, pavilions, and downtown streetscape.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Boca Raton lists Mizner Park at Federal Highway and Mizner Boulevard with fountains, walking paths, pavilions, benches, lighting, and hours from sunrise to 2 a.m.
cards.access_notes: The city lists the park as open sunrise–2 a.m. Alcohol and smoking are prohibited; parking includes metered spaces.

cards.title: Explore the coastal boardwalk
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning · Barrier island
cards.notes: Walk the coastal-forest boardwalk, climb Jacob’s Outlook if conditions allow, and leave wildlife undisturbed throughout the visit.
cards.short_summary: A marine and coastal-habitat stop connected to FAU research and local conservation.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Boca Raton describes Gumbo Limbo as a 20-acre coastal preserve with a boardwalk, butterfly garden, outdoor aquariums, Jacob’s Outlook, and an FAU research gallery.
cards.access_notes: The city currently lists trails, boardwalk, and tower from 7 a.m. to sunset; aquarium and gallery schedules differ. Groups require reservations.

cards.title: Finish beside the Atlantic
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · Spanish River Park
cards.notes: Use the park’s designated beach access, check posted water and weather conditions, and keep the final stop within guarded public areas.
cards.short_summary: A straightforward oceanfront finale at a named city park near campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Boca Raton’s official facility page states that Spanish River Park provides access to the beach and Atlantic Ocean.
cards.access_notes: Review current city notices, beach conditions, facility hours, and parking requirements before departure; follow all posted safety directions.

warnings: Schedules, exhibitions, shuttle service, recreation eligibility, parking charges, and coastal conditions can change; the linked direct sources should be rechecked before each stop.
Coordinates and map URLs are null where they were not independently verified from a direct authoritative page during this research pass.
